Build me a screening dashboard like https://focusalpha.ai/screener-dashboard, on my own filters.
Sample page: https://focusalpha.ai/screener-dashboard  ·  its full source: https://github.com/focusAlpha/dashboards/blob/main/screener-dashboard/index.html
The sample's data is frozen as of 2026-09-23. Mine must fetch live, through the connector.

FIRST look at the data, before writing any page:
1. Call screen_companies({ list_facets: true }) — it is free and it gives the exact spelling of
   every country, sector, exchange and event family, with the row counts behind each.
2. Call screen_companies once with my conditions below and read one row in full. Do not guess
   field names or units: margins, yields and growth come back as FRACTIONS (0.15 = 15%) while
   the price returns come back as percents.

THEN build it as an artifact that FETCHES ITS OWN DATA LIVE — not a page with the rows you
just pasted into it. That part is what makes it a dashboard instead of a screenshot:

- declare the connector when you publish the artifact:
    capabilities: { mcp: { servers: [{ server: "FocusAlpha", tools: ["screen_companies"] }] } }
  Without this declaration window.claude.use('mcp') resolves null and the page can never fetch.
- in the page:
    const mcp = await window.claude.use('mcp');
  It also resolves null for a viewer with no FocusAlpha connector — say that on the page
  rather than rendering an empty table.
- call a tool with:
    const r = await mcp.callTool("FocusAlpha", "<tool>", input, { cache: { staleTime: 120000 } });
    const payload = r.payload;
  Failures reject with an error carrying a code; render a sentence per code (not connected,
  needs sign-in, rate limited) instead of a blank screen.
- every control re-runs the call, debounced about 200ms, with a visible loading state.

What the page needs:
- a left rail of filters, one control per API parameter, with the parameter name printed under
  each label so I can see exactly what the control sends
- a table: ticker, company, country, sector, market cap, 1M / 3M / 12M return, guidance
  good-news and bad-news counts, and the 90-day event tags. Clicking a header re-sorts it
  through the API, not in the browser
- the exact call the page is sending, shown above the table
- coverage.refreshed_at printed on the page; missing values shown as "—", never as 0
- keep two things apart in separate columns: a guidance RAISE means a number went up, GOOD NEWS
  means better for the company. A cost line raised is a raise AND bad news.

My conditions (edit these):
  market_cap_usd_gte: 5000000000
  guidance_better_90d_gte: 1
  ret_3m_lte: 0
  sort: "guidance_better_90d"
